the דתניא at 134a.15-16 reporting R' Natan's two stories
adduces the baraita (דתניא) for the red/pale-baby rule

props.gloss_en: a baby whose exit is not known: let one rub it with oil and stand it toward the daylight
and where it is translucent, let one tear it with a barley grain lengthwise and widthwise
but not with a metal implement, because it causes swelling
a baby who does not suck: it is that his mouth is cold
what is his remedy? let them bring a cup of coals and hold it toward his mouth, so his mouth warms and he sucks
a baby who does not urinate: let one shake him in a sieve, and he urinates
a baby who does not breathe: let them bring his mother's afterbirth and rub it over him, and he breathes
a baby who is small: let them bring his mother's afterbirth and rub it over him from the narrow [end] to the wide
and if he is large -- from the wide to the narrow
a baby who is red -- [it is] that his blood has not yet been absorbed in him
let them wait for him until his blood is absorbed in him, and then circumcise him
a pale one -- [it is] that his blood has not yet entered him
let them wait until his blood enters him, and then circumcise him
R' Natan, in the coastal cities: [the third son of a woman whose first two died of circumcision] -- I saw that he was red; I said to her: wait for him until his blood is absorbed in him
she waited for him until his blood was absorbed in him, circumcised him, and he lived
and they would call him Natan the Babylonian after my name

R' Natan, in Cappadocia: [the third son of a woman whose first two died of circumcision] -- I saw that he was pale; I looked at him and saw no covenant blood in him; I said to her: wait for him until his blood enters him
and she waited for him, circumcised him, and he lived
and they would call his name Natan the Babylonian after my name
